exposure: admission to the intensive care unit
cohort: 1,015 healthy pregnant women aged between 18 and 45 years
finding: Health-related quality of life was higher after vaginal delivery than cesarean section, and factors like spousal support, regular sleep, and physical activity during pregnancy also contributed to better health-related quality of life.
mod_finding: Health-related quality of life was higher after vaginal delivery than after cesarean section, with emergency cesarean section having the lowest and elective cesarean section the second lowest scores.
